title: Financial Reporting Around Private Firms' Securities Offerings

scopes.description: Complete supplied R cleaning and prediction work plus the Stata master analysis workflow, including cross-language inputs, required raw-source construction and all referenced analysis branches.

requirements.description: SEC Form D raw tables read by R Part 1. The program selects submission, issuer, offering and recipient files; public table/field documentation supports these source products, while the in-code bindings for primary_issuers and offering remain a separate source issue.

routes.description: The official SEC product provides quarterly structured Form D tables, with a documented Jan 2008-to-current scope, tab-delimited UTF-8 files and ACCESSIONNUMBER/sequence keys. The R code reads SUBMISSION, ISSUERS, OFFERING and RECIPIENTS files; stage the files under its relative Data/RawData/Form D root and confirm headers/period during authorized preparation. The authors’ 2021 download date is provenance, not a byte-identity requirement.
routes.expected_period: SEC Form D submissions from Jan 2008 through the applicable quarterly product; the supplied code does not specify a fixed endpoint.

routes.description: The datasheet says survey responses are anonymous and personal information is confidential, with aggregate reporting. It does not establish a permanent denial or the terms for sharing the analysis file; obtain an authorized analysis-use copy and schema if needed.

The local COMP.FUNDA candidate contains SICH rather than the code’s SIC name; the actual definition/time mapping and prepared-file producer remain unresolved.

routes.description: The one-row probe confirms local annual Compustat fields GVKEY, DATADATE, FYEAR, FYR, AT, CEQ, CSHPRI, XRD, SICH and PRCC_F. Do not treat historical SICH as the code’s SIC without the source/dictionary meaning and time contract; this is a specific definition gap, not a generic library/path mismatch.

Other local actual/estimate products are candidates only; keep ibes.dta separate until its producer and measure definition are documented.
routes.expected_period: I/B/E/S history matched to the Compustat annual and event dates; the required date coverage is not specified.

issues.description: The Stata master clears all in-memory data and immediately generates information_count from pre-existing disclosure variables. No initial analysis dataset or producer is identified before this use, so the first Stata analysis block has an unresolved input handoff.
R_Code.R contains empty setwd settings before its relative raw-data and survey paths. The working-copy root and output directories must be set coherently before a future run.
R calls fread and parse_date_time before any package library statements and does not visibly attach data.table or lubridate. A clean entry session needs those namespaces loaded before first use.

The issuer and offering files are parsed into a generic all_files list, but the later joins use primary_issuers and offering objects. Their table-binding, primary-issuer selection and broker join-key construction are not established by the supplied R statements.
R reads the CSV into cb but later joins against cb_company; no producer for cb_company is visible. Its field preparation and identifier/name/state matching contract remain unknown.

The R branch reads survey.dta and a separate CSV named survey, while Stata reads survey data.dta. The package does not establish that these are the same source, compatible exports or the same analysis sample.

The Stata industry branch consumes SIC, while local COMP.FUNDA metadata exposes SICH, a historical SIC field. The source/dictionary definition and time contract needed to compare them are not established; do not automatically rename SICH to SIC.
Stata merges a separate ibes.dta file on PERMNO and DATADATE, then consumes EADATE and SURP. The producer, EPS measure and mapping from available I/B/E/S products to those variables are unknown.

Two connected Stata blocks remain wholly withheld by the required byte-first source screen. The adjacent erc_ff.dta and survey_website.dta consumers are known, but the hidden text is not used to infer their producers or other dependencies.

evidence.description: The ERC branch consumes daily CRSP identifiers and filters by share/exchange codes.

evidence.description: The ERC branch consumes RET, VWRETD and PRC to calculate market-adjusted returns and lagged price.
evidence.quote:
gen r = ln(1+ret)
gen v = ln(1+vwretd)
gen ret3d = l1.r+r+f1.r
gen vwret3d = l1.v+v+f1.v

replace ret3d = exp(ret3d)-1
replace vwret3d = exp(vwret3d)-1

gen aret3d = ret3d - vwret3d // abnormal return
label var aret3d "Market Adjusted 3-day Return (centered)"

replace prc = abs(prc)
gen prcl2d = l2.prc
label var prcl2d "Price at d-2"

evidence.description: Stata reads the Compustat annual alias, renames LPERMNO to PERMNO and merges the IBES and daily-return aliases.
evidence.quote:
use "./Data/Original/Compu_annual.dta", clear
rename *, lower
egen start = min(datadate), by(lpermno)
egen end   = max(datadate), by(lpermno)
bys lpermno: keep if _n==1
format %td start end
keep lpermno start end
save "./Data/Identifiers/ID_Compu_annual.dta", replace

use "./Data/Original/Compu_annual.dta", clear
rename *, lower

ren lpermno permno
gen matchdate = mofd(datadate)

merge 1:1 permno datadate using "./Data/Output/ibes.dta", keep(1 3) nogenerate

replace matchdate = eadate
replace matchdate = _n*10000 if matchdate == .
merge 1:1 permno matchdate using "./Data/Output/dailyreturns.dta", keep(1 3) nogenerate

evidence.quote:
In this section, I detail the steps taken to predict the information provision for non-respondent
Form D filers.
   Step 1: Defining the Predicted Variable
   I predict Information Provision index, the same variable used in previous analyses.
   Step 2: Identifying Predictors and Fit the Model
   I use two predictors: firm size and industry classification. For firm size, since firm asset or

revenue numbers are not available, I use two alternative continuous variables: the offering amount
and the number of investors. Both variables highly correlate with firm size, as larger firms typically
raise more funding and engage with more investors.
   Step 3: Fit the Linear Model and Obtain Coefficients of Predictors
   Using the survey sample, I fit a linear model with the previously identified predictors of private
disclosure. To ensure a sufficient sample size for prediction, I estimate the regression separately
for the three industries with over 30 observations: Technology, Healthcare, and Other.
   Step 5: Employ Bootstrapping for Robustness
   Given the relatively small sample size for each industry, I also employ a bootstrapping approach.
This method involves “re-sampling with replacement” all data points 1,000 times to estimate coef-
ficients. I then take the median value of these repeated estimates as the bootstrapping coefficients.
   Step 6: Predict Information Provision
   I use the coefficients estimated from both the original and bootstrapped models to predict the
Information Provision for Form D firms that do not participate in the survey.

review_notes: The assessed target is the full supplied R cleaning/prediction work and Stata master workflow. No separate analysis-only route is supported by a complete compatible prepared input; the first Stata block’s initial dataset remains an explicit unresolved handoff.

Source programs were screened byte-first before display. Exact source quotes use the saved screened reader. Two Stata connected blocks remain withheld; their contents and any producers within them are not inferred. The R Part 3 formd_cb_stata.dta output is retained as a supplied branch, but no visible Stata consumer is established. The two Stata dailyreturns products have different fields and roles and remain distinct.

Local catalog and one-row metadata evidence identifies CRSP daily/monthly stock, index and name-history products plus Compustat Funda, CCM and I/B/E/S candidates. One-row field metadata does not establish row coverage or empirical period coverage. CRSP path/format staging is preparation; Compustat SICH is not renamed to SIC; ibes.dta remains a separate unverified measure/producer mapping.

The SEC public Form D product and static documentation support the public raw-table route. The author-described DFPI batch product remains unverified: bounded official pages/snippets document filing/forms, while direct static-page requests returned HTTP 403 without bodies. That retrieval result is not treated as a data-access barrier or as proof of data absence. Survey privacy language is treated as an access/terms question, not permanent denial.

No author program, dataset payload, statistical/model trial, SAS process, source edit or remote job was run. Bounded metadata requests with wrong paths/field selections and their corrections were preserved as separate artifacts; the malformed original catalog-failure capture was not replaced. One quote-capture JSON verification command used an unavailable generic python alias; the saved quote file was subsequently parsed and hashed with the documented Miniforge interpreter.

The first saved metadata preflight found duplicate evidence rows, three dangling inherited scope references and a non-schema requirement-kind token. The duplicate rows were identical and deduplicated; the dangling references were removed because the current scope already cites the replacement evidence; every requirement kind now uses the frozen schema token. The failed preflight artifact is preserved.
